results.question: What is defamation under IPC section 499?

citations.quote: Whoever makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said, except in cases in which it is proved that such imputation is true, to have defamed that person.

baseline.answer:
Defamation under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) is defined as the act of making or publishing an imputation concerning another person, with the intention or knowledge that the imputation will harm that person's reputation, or with the recklessness that it will likely harm their reputation.

The specific legal provision states:

[[IPC s.499 | "Whoever makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said, except in cases in which it is proved that such imputation is true, to have defamed that person."]]

This section establishes that for an act to constitute defamation, the imputation must be made or published, it must concern a specific person, and the actor must have the requisite mental state (intention, knowledge, or reason to believe) that the act will harm the reputation of that person. The provision also includes a proviso that the imputation must not be true, as truth is a defense against defamation.

citations.quote: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said, except in the cases hereinafter excepted, to defame that person.

No imputation is said to harm a person's reputation, unless that imputation directly or indirectly, in the estimation of others, lowers the moral or intellectual character of that person, or lowers the character of that person in respect of his caste or of his calling, or lowers the credit of that person, or causes it to be believed that the body of that person is in a lothsome state, or in a state generally considered as disgraceful.

It may amount to defamation to impute anything to a deceased person, if the imputation would harm the reputation of that person if living, and is intended to be hurtful to the fellings of his family or other near relatives.
It may amount to defamation to make an imputation concerning a company or an association or collection of persons as such.
An imputation in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically, may amount to defamation.
